chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, regarding the saying of
Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “And We had certainly given a covenant to Adam before, but he forgot, and We did not find in him determination.”

He عليه السلام said: “We covenanted with him regarding Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and the Imams after him, but he left it, and there was not in him determination that they were thus. And the possessors of determination were only named the possessors of determination because He covenanted with them regarding Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, the successors after him, al-Mahdī عليه السلام, and his way; and their determination was united upon that it was so, and upon acknowledging it.”

key_terms.آدَمَ: Adam, the first human and prophet addressed in the verse
key_terms.أُولُو الْعَزْمِ: the possessors of determination; prophets distinguished by firm resolve
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةِ: the Imams; the divinely appointed leaders after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.الْأَوْصِيَاءِ: the successors; those appointed after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.الْإِقْرَارِ: acknowledgment; affirming and admitting the truth of the covenant
key_terms.الْمَهْدِيِّ: al-Mahdī عليه السلام, the guided Imam mentioned in the covenant
key_terms.عَزْمًا: determination; firmness and resolve in upholding the covenant
key_terms.عَهِدْنَا: We gave a covenant; a divine pledge or charge entrusted by Allah

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith interpret the covenant of Adam in Qur'an 20:115?
ai.summary: This report presents the verse as referring to a covenant taken from Adam concerning Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, the Imams after him, and the acknowledgment of their appointed status. It also explains that the prophets known as Ulu al-ʿAzm were given this title because they firmly upheld and affirmed this covenant. The passage is significant in linking the verse to wilayah, succession, and steadfast acknowledgment of divine appointment.
